thread:
kevin: FYI rolled out opal-liteq-v1 (int4-ish config) to canary with streaming enabled. getting unexpected funcall parse failures. ~0.9% on last 2k calls.

anya: can you paste an example? streaming or batch?

kevin: streaming. snippets show truncated arrays and occasionally an extra comma before close. saved one here:
```
{"cmd":"create_ticket","args":[{"field":"desc","value":"disk full"},]
```
stream ended before final bracket.

lee: hmm, that trailing-comma pattern is weird. our JSON serializer shouldn't add commas. could be tokenizer chunk boundary cutting inside multi-byte token or decoding artifact after quant kernels.

samir: did you compare to the fp16 baseline with identical prompts+seed?

kevin: yes. fp16 streaming on same workload: 0.05% parse failures. opal-liteq batch-mode: 0.12%. so streaming+liteq amplifies it.

anya: immediate quick fixes: 1) enable "json-sentinel" post-processor that waits for a closing brace/array or TTL before handing to funcall parser; 2) for canary, disable auto-retry-on-parse-fail to avoid duplicate tool calls; 3) mirror live traffic to fp16 for comparison.

lee: agree. add instrumentation: per-chunk sha1 and chunk-length, and record tokenization offsets. will help see whether chunks differ at the generator (model) or in transport.

kevin: adding a tiny assembler is low-risk. propose TTL=150ms for canary (latency impact small). if assembler sees obvious corruption (bad UTF-8 or unmatched braces) it should escalate a flag instead of retrying the tool.

ops-bot: mirrored traffic job queued: mirror/opal-liteq-v1->fp16/1722223333 (5k). will publish results to /ci/mirror/1722223333-report.json once done.

anya: longer term: unit-test the quant kernels with synthetic token streams that simulate JSON heavy outputs (deep nesting, long arrays). run with same seeds and compare per-token outputs. if mismatch appears before transport we know kernel distortion is culprit.

samir: also try alternative quant recipe: per-channel scaling + clamp adjustments. re-run small benchmark to check perf delta. include throughput, p50/p95 latency, and parse_failure_rate.

lee: for the canary I'll push a patch that gates streaming for opal-liteq-v1: if response_size > 1k bytes, fall back to buffered (non-chunked) streaming to avoid mid-token chop. small hack but might cut failures.

kevin: done. paused the canary streaming rollout and switched to buffered fallback. putting a short postmortem ticket: INF-3580. assigning to @lee and @samir.

anya: nice. once mirror job lands let's meet and decide whether to revert the model or keep disabled-streaming and iterate on quant config.

ops-bot: mirror report posted: /ci/mirror/1722223333-report.json (parse_failure_rate: opal-liteq-streaming=0.92%, opal-liteq-buffered=0.11%, fp16-streaming=0.04%). checksum-diff metric suggests per-token divergence starting ~token 42 on failing cases.

samir: checksum divergence points to generation-level difference. next: run per-layer ablation on quant scale to find offending layers. I'll spin up a small grid and post results.

kevin: thanks all. small wins: assembler + disabling retries removed duplicate invokes from our canary metric. will follow up with bench numbers when grid done. :rocket:
